title: Did Polaris Just Turn Into a Drone Stock?
content:
This week was a good week to own Polaris(NYSE: PII) stock -- and the next 52 weeks could be even better.

The manufacturer of everything from snowmobiles to motorcycles to all-terrain vehicles to boats reported first-quarter earnings on Tuesday, you see, crushing analyst forecasts and reporting a $0.13-per-share profit where Wall Street expected a loss of $0.40. Quarterly sales exceeded expectations as well, growing 8% year over year to $1.7 billion, and Polaris expanded its gross profit margin by 420 basis points to 20.2%.

Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue »Polaris builds ATVs -- now also for the U.S. military. Image source: Polaris.

Wall Street reacts

Analysts praised the results, and no fewer than six separate analysts raised their price targets on Polaris stock to between $60 a share (the most pessimistic, Wells Fargo) and $74 a share (the most optimistic -- Bank of America). Curiously, though, almost all of these analysts (the exception being Raymond James) maintained only neutral or hold ratings on Polaris stock.

The news might have been good enough to win some price target hikes -- but it wasn't good enough to convince most analysts to buy Polaris stock.

Why not?

The trouble with Polaris

Two factors may explain this. First and foremost, while Polaris "beat earnings" and reported positive non-GAAP (adjusted) profits, its actual earnings per share calculated under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) showed an $0.83-per-share loss for the quarter.

Second and related, Polaris guided investors to expect essentially zero sales growth through the end of this year. Sales are expected to be about $7.2 billion in 2026 -- the same as in 2025. For Polaris to win higher ratings from Wall Street and more investor support, it seems the company must find a way to grow its sales faster.

Fortunately, Polaris may have a plan for that -- and it comes from an unexpected direction.Image source: Forterra.

Uncle Sam wants Polaris

Earlier this week, Maryland-based defense start-up Forterra unveiled the new Mesa Autonomous Ground Vehicle (essentially a drone truck, rather than a drone aircraft) that it's developing for the U.S. Army -- with help from Polaris.

Guided by software and capable of maneuvering autonomously even in areas where GPS signals are jammed, Mesa, according to Forterra, is based on a "factory modified Polaris Ranger XD 1500 all-terrain vehicle."

Although the photo Forterra provided shows Mesa to be about twice as long as a base Ranger XD 1500, Forterra explains that Mesa is "built in direct partnership with Polaris" and that "every vehicle comes off the same market-leading production line that delivers" Polaris's other vehicles.

Story Continues

Translation: Forterra is working with Polaris to build this new military robot. The more successful Forterra is in selling it, the more it will directly benefit Polaris through improved sales and (ideally) a return to positive profits.

Keep an eye on Forterra

As for Polaris's partner in this venture, investors might also want to keep a close eye on Forterra, which is starting to seem like a real up-and-comer (even if most people have never heard of it).

Defense website Tectonic calls Forterra "a giant in the ground autonomy game" and earning praise for its AutoDrive vehicle autonomy system, which includes all the hardware, software, and sensors necessary to convert essentially any existing vehicle into an autonomous ground drone. In addition to Polaris, Forterra has also teamed up with big-league defense contractors such as BAE Systems, General Dynamics, Oshkosh, and Rheinmetall in Germany to produce autonomous ground vehicles.

The company also recently hit unicorn status, raising hundreds of millions in venture capital financing and achieving a private market valuation of $1.1 billion. With any luck, an initial public offering may not be too far off.

title: Polaris Inc (PII) Q1 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Strong Sales Growth and Margin Improvements ...
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Revenue: Sales up 8% or 14% organically, excluding Indian Motorcycle. Adjusted EPS: $0.13, exceeding expectations; $0.26 excluding Indian Motorcycle. Power Sports Segment Growth: Double-digit growth led by utility RANGER line and Snowmobiles. North American Retail Growth: 1% overall, with ORV up 3%. Gross Margin Improvement: Increased by 389 basis points despite 240 basis points tariff headwind. Adjusted EBITDA Margin: Increased by 277 basis points. Snowmobile Retail Growth: 25% growth for the '25-'26 season. Marine Segment: Retail down low double digits; strong mix of premium pontoons. Dealer Inventory: Healthy levels, with snowmobile inventory down over 50% from last year. Free Cash Flow: First quarter cash flow better than planned, despite being a net outflow. Dividend Growth: 31st consecutive year of dividend growth. Debt Reduction: Over $530 million reduced during 2025. Tariff Costs: Expected total of approximately $215 million for the year.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 7 Warning Signs with PII. Is PII fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: April 28, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.

Positive Points

Polaris Inc (NYSE:PII) reported an 8% increase in sales, or 14% organically, excluding Indian Motorcycle impacts. The company delivered an adjusted EPS of $0.13, exceeding expectations. Polaris Inc (NYSE:PII) achieved double-digit growth in its Power Sports segment, driven by the utility RANGER line and snowmobiles. Gross margins improved by 389 basis points despite a 240 basis point headwind from tariffs. The company gained market share in both ORV and Snow categories for the fourth consecutive quarter.

Negative Points

Geopolitical tensions and rising oil prices led to a decline in retail performance starting in mid-March. Marine retail was down in the first quarter, with a low double-digit decline according to the SSI report. Tariffs posed a 240 basis point headwind in the quarter, impacting overall financial performance. The recreational category continues to be challenged, with retail down high single digits. Uncertainty around consumer behavior and evolving tariff policies are causing caution in future outlooks.

Q & A Highlights

Q: Could you help us unpack your tariff exposure in guidance after the IEEPA ruling and including recent Section 232 changes? A: Michael Speetzen, CEO, explained that the tariff impact remains around $215 million. The Supreme Court ruling on IEEPA tariffs and the subsequent 122 tariff changes resulted in a $40 million benefit. However, the Section 232 changes offset this benefit. The company is working to reduce China-sourced content to below 5% by the end of 2027, which should help mitigate future tariff impacts.

Story Continues

Q: How do you see the competitive environment evolving in light of the tariff changes? A: Michael Speetzen, CEO, noted that while tariffs impact costs, there is limited price elasticity in the market. The focus remains on product innovation and regaining market share, with Polaris gaining share for four consecutive quarters in the ORV segment. The company is confident in its product portfolio and its ability to compete effectively.

Q: Given the strong first-quarter performance, why not raise full-year guidance? A: Michael Speetzen, CEO, stated that despite strong performance, the company is taking a conservative approach due to uncertainties around consumer behavior and tariff policies. If the consumer environment remains stable and no new tariffs are introduced, there could be potential upside to the current guidance.

Q: Can you provide more details on the operational improvements contributing to ORV gross margin? A: Robert Mack, CFO, highlighted that volume and mix were the biggest drivers of margin improvement, followed by net pricing and plant performance. The company expects these operational efficiencies to continue benefiting margins throughout the year.

Q: What is the impact of the distressed supplier adjustment on financials? A: Robert Mack, CFO, explained that the $22.5 million adjustment was related to supporting a supplier through bankruptcy to ensure continuity of supply. This was a one-time impact and demonstrates Polaris's commitment to maintaining supply chain stability.

title: Polaris Inc. Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Polaris Inc. Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance Drivers

Performance exceeded expectations driven by double-digit growth in the utility RANGER line and commercial business, offsetting continued weakness in the recreational category. Gross margin expansion of 389 basis points was achieved through favorable product mix, net pricing, and lean manufacturing efficiencies, despite a 240 basis point headwind from tariffs. Management attributes the 14% organic sales growth to a strategic focus on the utility segment, which now represents 70% of Off-Road Vehicle (ORV) revenue. Operational improvements are linked to the 'lean journey,' with factory utilization increasing toward 70% and structural savings reaching over $240 million. Market dynamics showed a mid-March retail dip correlated with geopolitical tensions and oil prices, followed by a return to growth across most categories in April. The earlier-than-expected closure of the Indian Motorcycle separation has allowed management to refocus on its core Powersports and Marine segments, with the separation expected to be accretive to adjusted EBITDA.

Outlook and Strategic Assumptions

Guidance assumes a relatively flat retail environment for the remainder of 2026, with production and shipments strictly aligned to retail demand to maintain healthy dealer inventory. The tariff mitigation strategy aims to reduce China-sourced material costs from 14% to below 5% by the end of 2027 through supply chain localization. Financial results are expected to return to historic seasonal patterns, with the second and third quarters projected as the highest revenue and EPS periods. Management is maintaining a prudent outlook due to external uncertainties, including potential changes to USMCA and Section 301 trade policies and volatile consumer sentiment. The Indian Motorcycle separation is expected to be accretive by approximately $50 million to adjusted EBITDA, with impacts weighted toward the second half of the year.

Risk Factors and Structural Changes

Total tariff costs for 2026 are projected at approximately $215 million, with recent Section 232 changes effectively offsetting benefits from the IEEPA ruling. A $22.5 million one-time adjustment was recorded to support a distressed supplier through bankruptcy to ensure component continuity and protect future margins. Commodity headwinds, specifically in steel and diesel, are expected to double from initial $20 million estimates to over $40 million for the full year. Polaris intends to seek refunds for approximately $125 million in IEEPA tariffs paid previously, though this potential benefit is excluded from current guidance.

Story Continues

Q&A Highlights

Net impact of Section 232 and IEEPA tariff changes

Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.

Management confirmed that a $40 million benefit from the IEEPA ruling was almost perfectly offset by a $40 million headwind from new Section 232 tariffs. The impact of Section 232 is felt almost immediately because dealer inventory has already been recognized as revenue and is being replenished daily.

Competitive dynamics and price elasticity in the current market

Management believes there is limited price elasticity remaining in the market following significant post-COVID price increases. The strategy focuses on product innovation and market share gains rather than aggressive pricing maneuvers to offset competitor cost structures.

Structural versus cyclical changes in the recreational segment

Management views the current recreational slowdown as cyclical rather than structural, noting that vehicle usage metrics like oil and parts consumption remain high. The 'want' nature of recreational products makes consumers more sensitive to macro stability, leading to an extended replenishment cycle that management expects will eventually normalize.

Operating expense timing and full-year expectations

Approximately $30 million in operating expenses were pulled forward into Q1 due to the timing of corporate costs and higher incentive compensation accruals. Management expects these costs to normalize over the remaining three quarters, keeping full-year OpEx within original guidance ranges.

title: Polaris Inc (PII) Q1 Earnings and Revenues Beat Estimates

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +130.37%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this snowmobile and ATV maker would post earnings of $0.06 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.08, delivering a surprise of +33.33%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Polaris Inc, which belongs to the Zacks Automotive - Domestic industry, posted revenues of $1.66 billion for the quarter ended March 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.38%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.54 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Polaris Inc shares have lost about 3.5% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 4.8%.

What's Next for Polaris Inc?

While Polaris Inc has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Polaris Inc was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock.
